title: A PVT-Robust 5.5GHz Fractional-N Cascaded RO-Based Digital PLL with Voltage-Domain Feedforward Noise Cancellation
problem: Ring-oscillator (RO)-based digital PLLs (DPLLs) offer compactness and immunity to magnetic coupling but suffer from high phase noise limited by quantization noise (Q-noise) and RO phase-noise (PN_RO). Prior PN-suppression techniques are prone to PVT variations, energy inefficient, or require complex correlation-based calibration of gain and threshold delays.
motivation: Multi-PLL-integrated SoCs on modern processes require compact, PVT-robust, low-jitter PLLs for high-speed communication and clocking.
method: The design cascades ring oscillators in a fractional-N digital phase-locked loop—a circuit that synchronizes to frequencies by using flexible dividers instead of fixed integer ones. It converts time delays to voltages and digitizes them to suppress quantization noise while remaining reliable across manufacturing processes, voltages, and temperatures. A voltage-domain feedforward noise cancellation technique (measuring and subtracting noise before it accumulates) eliminates the need for complex gain calibration. This achieves 290.8 femtoseconds of jitter at 5.5GHz, with less than 7.5% variation across PVT conditions.
key_novelty: Voltage-domain feedforward noise cancellation eliminates the need for correlation-based gain calibration while suppressing phase noise robustly across process, voltage, and temperature variations, reducing power and design complexity.
contributions: 290.8fs rms jitter at 5.5GHz fractional-N frequency with -62dBc worst fractional spurs
PVT robustness: <7.5% jitter deviation across -20-100°C and ±5% V_DD variations
Voltage-domain feedforward noise cancellation without gain calibration, enabling fast delta-sigma-modulator restoration
limitations: Absolute area, power dissipation, and comparison with non-cascaded RO-PLLs or LC-based DPLLs not provided.
